extra.message: User-controlled input from the 'username' query parameter (defined on line 8) is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string and rendered via Jinja2.from_string(...).render(). Because the user input becomes part of the template source rather than being passed as a rendering context variable, an attacker can inject Jinja2 template expressions. For example, requesting '/?username={{7*7}}' returns 'Welcome 49!', and using a default (unsandboxed) jinja2.Environment allows access to Python object internals (e.g. {{ ''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__() }}) leading to arbitrary code / OS command execution and full server compromise. This is a classic Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI).

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
